title: Register a birth
kw: register birth baby born newborn birth registration civil registration registrar nascimento bebê registrar
short: Every birth in Ireland must be registered within 3 months. It is free, and many parents can now do it online.
facts: Online or any Civil Registration Office
need: The birth notification ID you were given for the birth.
Each parent’s details: PPS number, address at the time of the birth, occupation, civil status and the mother’s maiden name.
To register online, each parent needs a verified [MyGovID](#/s/mygovid).
steps: Go to **Civil Registration Services** online and sign in with MyGovID, or visit any Civil Registration Office: it does not have to be near where the baby was born.
Enter the birth notification ID and the parents’ and baby’s details.
After registration the baby is given a PPS number automatically.
Order a [birth certificate](#/s/certificates): you will need it for school enrolment, a passport and other purposes.

a: If your marriage is on record in Ireland, one parent can complete the whole registration online. The other parent does not need a verified MyGovID.

Registration online has two parts and the mother starts it; then the father completes his part. Since 10 December 2025 an unmarried mother must give the father’s contact details, unless there is a compelling reason not to name him.

Some births cannot be registered online and must be done at a Civil Registration Office: for example donor-assisted births, stillbirths, where a parent has died, or where the mother is widowed, divorced or separated.

cases.q: We want to change or add a first name later
a: Adding or changing a forename costs €5. Re-registering to add a parent’s details is free.

title: Get married in Ireland
kw: get married marriage wedding notification of intention to marry registrar civil ceremony casar casamento marriage registration form
short: You must both meet a registrar at least 3 months before the wedding to give notice. It costs €200, and this applies to everyone, Irish or not.
facts: Give notice at least 3 months ahead
who: Any couple, same sex or opposite sex, where both people are 18 or over and free to marry.
need: Passport (original and a colour photocopy of the photo page), or an EU national identity card. It must be in date.
Proof of address dated in the last 3 months, original and photocopy.
Your PPS numbers, if you have them.
The completed [booking form](https://assets.gov.ie/static/documents/marriage-notification-appointment-booking-form.pdf), with your ceremony date, venue, solemniser and two witnesses aged 18 or over.
Official translations of any document that is not in English or Irish.
steps: Book a notification appointment: [online for a civil ceremony](https://www2.hse.ie/services/births-deaths-and-marriages/getting-married/book-appointment/) in most areas, or by phoning a civil registration service. Appointments fill quickly.
Both of you attend, show your documents, pay €200 and sign a declaration that there is no legal reason you cannot marry.
If everything is in order, the registrar gives you a **Marriage Registration Form**. You cannot marry without it.

Hold the ceremony with a solemniser who is on the [Register of Solemnisers](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-social-protection/publications/register-of-solemnisers/). For a civil ceremony the registrar does this.
After a religious or secular ceremony, bring the signed form to any civil registration service within one month. Registering it is free.

cases.q: One of us is not Irish or not an EU citizen
a: You will have an interview with the registrar. If one of you is not an EU citizen, bring evidence of your immigration status.

cases.q: One of us was married before
a: Divorced: bring the original or a certified copy of the divorce decree. Foreign divorces are examined by the General Register Office, which takes extra time. Widowed: bring your civil marriage certificate and your late spouse’s death certificate.
Ask a civil registration service about giving notice by post. You still need 3 months’ notice and you must meet the registrar in person at least 5 days before the ceremony.

cases.q: We want the ceremony outside the registry office
a: A civil ceremony at another approved venue costs an additional fee.

title: Register a death and what to do next
kw: register death died bereavement funeral death certificate someone died widow probate will falecimento óbito morte
short: A death must be registered within 3 months. It is free and can be done with any registrar in the country. A short checklist of who else to tell is below.
need: The **Death Notification Form**. The doctor who attended the person completes Part 1, with the medical cause of death, and gives it to the family.
steps: Get the Death Notification Form from the doctor or hospital.
A relative, civil partner or other qualified person (for example someone who was present at the death) brings it to any [civil registration service](https://www2.hse.ie/births-deaths-and-marriages/).
Order [death certificates](#/s/certificates): you will need them to deal with the person’s affairs.
Tell the Department of Social Protection if the person was getting a payment, and Revenue about possible tax refunds or credits.
Notify banks, credit unions, pension and insurance providers, and cancel direct debits.
Contact the executor named in the will. If there is no will, an administrator must be appointed to deal with the estate.

a: After the coroner’s inquiry, the coroner sends a certificate to the civil registration service, which registers the death and tells the family when they can apply for a death certificate.

The death is registered in the country where it happened. In some cases you can ask for a [record of a death abroad](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-social-protection/services/record-of-death-abroad/) in Ireland.

cases.q: What about their passport and vote?
a: The passport can be returned to the Passport Service for cancellation. Ask the local authority to update the Register of Electors.
